 3.  Resolution Accepting a Grant from the State of California Department of Parks and
  Recreation Division of Boating Waterways Boating Safety and Enforcement Equipment
  Grant Program
  The City submitted a grant to the Division of Boating and Waterways Boating Safety and
  Enforcement Equipment Grant Program. The funding agency requires the City to provide
  a resolution stating the signatory on the grant agreement has the authority to enter into
  the agreement and is authorized to execute it.
  Recommended Action
  1. Adopt a resolution accepting a grant from the State of California Department of Parks
  and Recreation, Division of Boating and Waterways Boating Safety and Enforcement
  Equipment Grant Program. 2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the grant
  agreement.

4.  Civic Center Housing Project Request for Proposal for Site Work and Construction
  Phases
  On May 6, 2025 City Council approved awarding a contract to US-Offsite for Phase 1-
  Design and Phase 2 Manufacturing of Modular Housing Units, with the caveat to return
  -

  before proceeding with Phase 2 to determine financial project feasibility. To gain the
  clearest picture of project feasibility, City staff recommends issuing a RFP for Phase 3A,
  foundational site work and a second REP for Phase 3B, installation of the modular units.
  Both REPs will include explicit language that award is contingent upon project financing
  and City Council award.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize City staff to publish two Civic Center Housing Project requests for proposal for
  on-site civil preparation work and for modular unit construction.

5.  Storm Drain Pipe Equipment Procurement for Hiawatha Sinkhole
  To repair a sinkhole on Hiawatha Avenue, City Staff propose the replacement of a 99-
  foot expanse of pipe.
  Recommended Action
  Per the City of Avalon’s Purchasing Policy, authorize the City Manager, or his designee,
  to purchase 36-inch Snap-Tite® pipe from Stormwater Experts for a not-to-exceed sum
  of $50,000 from CIP Fund #205010, Account #1245-6547.

GENERAL BUSINESS

6.  First Reading of an Ordinance to Repeal and Replace Chapter 1-8 (Reasonable
  Accommodation) of Title 1 of the Avalon Municipal Code, Implementing Housing Program
  17 as set forth in the 6” Cycle General Plan Housing Element and Adoption of Exemption
  Findings Under the California Environmental Quality Act
  Reasonable accommodation procedures ensure disabled persons have equal and
  effective access to City programs and services, and that reasonable and long-term
  modifications to City employment, building, and zoning rules, regulations, practices, and
  standards may be made for disabled persons to the extent required under federal and

  state disability laws, including but not limited to the Americans With Disabilities Act,
  Federal Fair Housing Act and the California Fair Employment and Housing Act.
  Recommended Action
  Introduce and waive all readings of an ordinance of the City of Avalon to repeal and
  replace Chapter 1-8 (Reasonable Accommodation) of Title 1 of the Avalon Municipal
  Code, implementing housing program 17 as set forth in the 6tui Cycle General Plan
  Housing Element and adoption of exemption findings under the California Environmental
  Quality Act.

7.  Procurement of Shore Boat End Float
  Over the last several months, the City has engaged in general discussions with Scott
  Gorelczenko regarding potential sale of the Shore Boat Float and assignment of the
  remaining lease term.
  Recommended Action
  Pending inspections by City Staff and a third-party Marine Surveyor: 1. Authorize the City
  Manager to negotiate and execute a purchase agreement for the Summer End Float from
  Catalina Jet Ski Corporation for a not-to-exceed sum of $595,000. 2. Amend the Harbor
  Fund budget increasing the Fiscal Year 2025-26 Budget allocating $595,000 to Capital
  Outlay R and M Floats/Wharfs Fund #10470-6504, and $60,000 to Float Maintenance
  —  —

  Fund #10470-5705.

8.  Magical Cruise Company Ltd. Cruise Ship Preferential Access Agreement
  During the February 18, 2025 City Council Meeting, the City authorized the City Manager
  to execute a Term Sheet with Magical Cruise Company Ltd, dba Disney Cruise Lines.
  Negotiations with Disney Cruise Lines have resulted in an agreement addressing and
  incorporating all of the relevant terms previously established.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to execute a Preferential Access Agreement with Magical
  Cruise Company Ltd., dba Disney Cruise Line.

9.  Award Cost of Service Study for Sewer, Saltwater, and Solid Waste Enterprise Funds
  The City provides Sewer, Saltwater, and Solid Waste services to approximately 1,400
  residential and commercial parcels within the city limits. These utilities operate as
  enterprise funds, where rates and fees within each fund are set to cover the costs of
  providing the respective services to customers. The process for increasing rates is subject
  to Proposition 218. The most recent cost of service study included adopted service fees
  for the enterprise funds covering five (5) fiscal years ending June 30, 2026.
  Recommended Action
  1. Award contract and authorize City Manager to execute an agreement with HDR
  Engineering, Inc. (HDR) to provide a cost of service study for the City of Avalon’s Sewer,
  Saltwater, and Solid Waste Enterprise Funds for an amount not-to-exceed $68,530; 2.
  Amend the Solid Waste Fund budget increasing the Solid Waste professional services
  account (13125-5005) by $28,000 to cover its proportional share of the project costs.

10.  Cabrillo Mole Revitalization Project Phase  — Remainder of Work and Phase II Wharf
  —

  Infill Contract Award
  On October 22, 2024, the City Council approved the design plan and authorized
  procurement for Stage 0 of the Cabrillo Mole Revitalization Project. The City solicited a
  request for bids from qualified contractors to complete step 1 of Stage 0 completion of
  —

  the Phase I scope of work as well as installation of grates over the top of two existing cut
  outs along the easterly face of the Mole. The City received one bid by the stated deadline.
  Recommended Action
  Award contract to Slater Waterproofing, Inc. for the Revitalization Project Phase I  —

  Remainder of Work and Phase II  —  Wharf Infill Project for a not-to-exceed sum of
  $950,000.

11.  On-Call Consulting Services Contract Amendment for International Consulting Services,
  Inc.
  On May 6, 2025, the City Council authorized the City Manager to execute an agreement
  with International Consulting Services, Inc. for a three-year term and a not-to-exceed
  contract sum of $100,000 annually. As the City ramps up activities associated with its
  Workforce Housing and Cabrillo Mole Revitalization projects, ICS task orders for these
  projects has exceeded initial estimates. City Staff request a one-time authorization to
  increase the ICS professional services agreement.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to execute an amendment to the Professional Services
  Agreement with International Consulting Services, Inc. increasing contract services by
  $175,000, for a not-to-exceed 12-month contract sum of $275,000 for on-call project
  management services.

12.  Amendment to US-Offsite Agreement for Civic Center Housing Project to Include Traffic
  and Logistics Study
  The City Council awarded a contract to US-Offsite for the Civic Center Housing Project,
  authorizing Phase 1 with direction to return to Council prior to issuance of Phase 2. As
  part of Phase 1 planning and design work, it has been determined that a traffic and
  logistics study is necessary to evaluate the transport of oversized modular housing units
  from the barge landing through the City to the Civic Center campus.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to execute an amendment to the agreement with US-Offsite
  to include a Traffic and Logistics Study in an amount of $7,000 for the Civic Center
  Housing Project.

13.  Short-Term Rental Application Waitlist Policy Discussion
  On August 9, 2025, The City Council introduced and waived all further readings of an
  ordinance repealing and replacing Article 3 of Chapter 1 of Title 3 of the Avalon Municipal
  Code modifying the Transient Rental System. Per the City Council’s direction, the
  ordinance established a cap of 410 transient rental units within the City of Avalon and

  authorizes the City Manager to implement a policy to regulate the manner in which the
  Planning Commission considers new transient rental licenses once that limit is reached.
  Recommended Action
  Hear a presentation regarding policy options for processing short-term rental applications
  after the maximum number of licenses have been issued. If consensus, provide direction
  to City Staff.

SUBJECT:  Resolution Accepting a Grant from the State of California
  Department of Parks and Recreation Division of Boating Waterways
  Boating Safety and Enforcement Equipment Grant Program

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): 1. Adopt a resolution accepting a grant from the State of
California Department of Parks and Recreation, Division of Boating and Waterways Boating
Safety and Enforcement Equipment Grant Program. 2. Authorize the City Manager to execute
the grant agreement.

REPORT SUMMARY: The City submitted a grant application in April 2025 for two (2) new
Yamaha 150 HP Outboard Engines (including steering set) through the Division of Boating and
Waterways Boating Safety and Enforcement Equipment Grant Program.

The City was notified in late September that the grant request of $55,663.02 for the two outboard
engines was recommended for funding.

The funding agency requires the City to provide a resolution stating the signatory on the grant
agreement has the authority to enter into the agreement and is authorized to execute it.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Safety

FISCAL IMPACTS: None, there is no required match for the grant.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City will not receive
the grant funds.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Execute the contract and forward to the Department of Boating and
Waterways with the required Resolution.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: This item was properly listed on the posted
agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.

  WHEREAS, the City of Avalon is desirous of improving a boating infrastructure
grant facility at Avalon Harbor to meet the needs of the boaters and to provide public
access to these facilities; and

  WHEREAS, the Division of Boating and Waterways is authorized to provide grants
to cities, counties, districts, and other public agencies for the construction and
development of such facilities; and

  WHEREAS, the City of Avalon is willing to enter into an agreement with the
Department of Boating and Waterways to provide two Yamaha 150 horsepower outboard
engines to enhance public safety in Avalon Harbor; and

  NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the City Council of the City of Avalon

 7.  Three RECREATIONAL BOATING safety issues

  This is a Federal Pass-Through Recreational Boating Safety Grant’. The purpose of the grant is to promote
  boating safety and to decrease the number of accidents, injuries, and fatalities on U.S. waters. Clearly identify
  three BOATING safety issues that affect recreational boaters in your jurisdiction. Your answer to this question
  will be referenced throughout this grant application.
  High Density Boating Activities
  Avalon Bay is a recreational boater’s haven for thousands of visitors per year. These visitors enjoy
  the island’s waters on powerboats, dinghies, paddle boards, u-drive rental boats, kayaks, and
  swimming. While the Harbor Department welcomes these activities, the congestion can pose as an
  issue when trying to assist boaters on their moorings or in the event of an emergency. Patrol boats
  must be equipped with reliable engines that are spry enough to start and stop at a moment’s notice.

  •  Operator Inexperience
  Avalon is the furthest offshore incorporated port within the Southern California boating community.
  Many boat operators who visit have yet to develop the adequate skill of open-water pilotage. The
  combination of unskilled captains and vessels that are not equipped for the open-ocean
  environment can create a variety of hazards on the water. Harbor Patrol are the first on scene
  responders due to our remote location. Our boats must be prepared to maintain higher speeds for
  longer durations to assist with outer harbor incidents.

  •  Boating Under the Influence
  Many boaters come to Avalon in search of enjoying the slower island lifestyle and taking in the
  views of town from the back of their boats while enjoying their favorite afternoon beverage. For most
  boaters, this is how they start their evening before they make their way into town to enjoy dinner on
  shore, enjoy a nightcap at a local bar, and then re-board their dinghies to return to their boats for the
  night. One of the biggest safety issues we see is boating under the influence. This creates a variety
  of hazards both inside and outside the harbor. Harbor Patrol vessels must be quick and agile
  enough to assist in a dinghy calamity inside the harbor, but also capable of maintaining higher
  speeds for longer durations if an emergency were to occur outside the harbor.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Introduce by title only and waive all readings of an ordinance of
the City of Avalon to repeal and replace Chapter 1-8 (Reasonable Accommodation) of Title I of
the Avalon Municipal Code, implementing housing program 17 as set forth in the 6th Cycle
General Plan Housing Element and adoption of exemption findings under the California
Environmental Quality Act.

BACKGROUND: On September 20, 2022, the City Council adopted the 202 1-2029/6th Cycle
General Plan Housing Element. The Housing Element is a state-mandated section of the
General Plan which identifies the housing needs, opportunities, and constraints in the of City of
Avalon. The Housing Plan section of the Housing Element further sets forth the City’s goals,
policies and programs to address Avalon’s identified housing needs, including production of 27
new housing units as allocated by the Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG)
Regional Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA) for the 6th review cycle.

The Housing Plan contains 26 programs adopted to implement the goals and policies of the
Housing Element. Some programs require one-time code amendments, while others have
ongoing review schedules that require monitoring legislative actions and regular updates to the
Avalon Municipal Code (AMC). Over the next several months, the Planning and Building
Department will bring forth a series of code amendments for consideration to implement all of
the housing programs to ensure the City continues to be compliant with State law. The
amendments proposed at this time are intended to address the requirements of Program #17
(Reasonable Accommodation Procedures).

PROGRAM #17  - REASONABLE ACCOMMODATION PROCEDURES: Reasonable
accommodation procedures ensure disabled persons have equal and effective access to
City programs and services, and that reasonable and long-term modifications to City
employment, building, and zoning rules, regulations, practices, and standards may be made
for disabled persons to the extent required under federal and state disability laws, including but
not limited to the Americans With Disabilities Act (42 U.S.C. § 12101 et seq.), Federal Fair
Housing Act (42 U.S.C. § 3601 et seq.) and the California Fair Employment and Housing Act
(Cal. Gov’t Code § 12955 etseq.).

Households that include persons with disabilities are some of the community’s lower-income
households, as determined by the communitywide median household income survey
prepared with the 6” Cycle Housing Element. Providing reasonable accommodation
procedures in compliance with State law will address the needs of both persons with
 disabilities and lower-income households. Program #17 requires that the City review its
adopted reasonable accommodation procedures annually and revise them as appropriate
to ensure consistency with federal and state fair housing requirements.

Chapter 1-8 was last updated in 2014. After reviewing the existing reasonable
accommodation regulations, it was determined by staff that updates are required to clarify
the scope of the program and to streamline the process for application and approval of
requested accommodations. As such, staff recommends the City Council repeal and replace
Chapter 1-8 with completely updated regulations.

Complete ordinance language is included in the draft ordinance as Attachment I and the
existing regulations are included for reference as Attachment 2. It is the opinion of staff that the
proposed regulations fully implement Program #17 of the 6th Cycle Housing Element and provide
for more streamlined procedures and access to reasonable accommodation requests for the
corn mu n ity.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The Avalon Municipal
Code will not be amended, and the City will be out of compliance with the mandated
implementation program set forth in the 6th Cycle General Plan Housing Element.

§1-8.01 Purpose and Intent.
It is the policy of the City to make, as provided in this section, reasonable accommodation
in the application of its policies, practices, programs, and procedures, including its zoning
and land-use laws, for disabled persons, to the extent required under federal and state
disability laws, including but not limited to the Americans With Disabilities Act (42 U.S.C.
§ 12101 et seq.), Federal Fair Housing Act (42 U.S.C. § 3601 et seq.), and the
California Fair Employment and Housing Act (Cal. Gov’t Code § 12955 et seq.). The
purpose of this chapter is to establish a process for disabled persons to submit and for
the City to act upon a request for reasonable accommodation.

§1-8.02 Definitions
For the purposes of this section, unless otherwise apparent from the context, certain
words or phrases used in this section are defined as follows:
  a) “Auxiliary aids and services” means qualified interpreters, note takers,
  transcription services, written materials, assistive listening systems, qualified
  readers, taped texts, audio recordings, Braille materials, large print materials,
  other similar services and actions, and as otherwise defined by state or federal
  law.

  b) “Person with a disability” means a person who has a physical or mental impairment
  that makes achievement of a major life activity difficult, as defined by state and
  federal disability laws; anyone who is regarded as having such impairment; or
  anyone with a record of such impairment.

  c) “RA Request” means a request for a Reasonable Accommodation submitted by,
  or on behalf of, a person with a disability.

  d) “Reasonable Accommodation” means providing persons with disabilities flexibility
  in the application of city programs; including city land-use, zoning, and building
  regulations; policies; practices; and procedures, or waiving certain requirements
  when it is necessary to provide meaningful access to city programs or to eliminate
  barriers to housing opportunities for persons with disabilities.

  e) “Review Authority” means the city manager or the city manager’s designee. See
  Section 1-8.03 of this chapter.

§ 1-8.03 Review Authority
The City Manager or the City Manager’s designee has the authority to review and decide
upon requests for a RA Request. A denial of an RA Request may be appealed by the
req uestor to a designated hearing officer. The hearing officer’s decision is final.
§1-8.04 Applicability
  a) Eligibility.

  1. An RA Request may be made by any person with a disability, his or her
  representative, or a developer or provider of housing or other services for
  persons with disabilities, when the application of a city program, including a
  city land-use or building regulation, policy, practice or procedure, acts as a
  barrier to meaningful access to city programs or to fair-housing
  opportunities for persons with disabilities.

  2. Federal and state disability laws afford no protection to persons with or
  without disabilities whose tenancy presents a direct threat to the persons or
  property of others. Determining whether someone’s tenancy poses such a
  direct threat must be made on an individualized basis, however, and may
  not be based on general assumptions or speculation about the nature of a
  disability.

  b) Eligible Request. The subject matter of an RA Request may include a modification
  or exception to the practices, rules, or standards for a city program or for the
  development, siting, and use of housing or housing-related facilities that would
  eliminate regulatory barriers and provide a person with a disability with meaningful
  access to city programs and equal opportunity to housing of the person’s choice.

§ 1-8.05 Application
  a) Requirements. An RA Request may be initiated with the Review Authority orally or
  in writing. The City will not require a requestor to use a particular form or medium
  to initiate an RA Request. The law requires the Reasonable Accommodation
  process to be iterative and interactive. City staff will assist requestors in completing
  their RA Request as needed to ensure that the process is accessible to persons
  with disabilities. The City encourages requestors to make RA Requests for
  auxiliary aids and services up to 48 hours before the City event needing
  accommodation.

  b) Administration. The City may create any forms, documents, online portals,
  telephone hotlines, or other methods to facilitate the submittal of RA Requests.

§1-8.06 Review and Processing
  a) Application Review. The Review Authority will approve, approve with conditions,
  or deny an RA Request in accordance with the required findings in Section 1-8.07
  of this chapter.

  b) Decision.

  1. Request for Further Information. The Review Authority may request further
  information from the applicant consistent with state and federal disability
  laws and this section, specifying in detail the further information required.

  2. Decision and Timing. The Review Authority will issue a written decision
  within 30 days of its receipt of a complete RA Request (including any
  additional information requested under subsection b(1) above). The written
  decision must: explain in detail the basis of the decision under the required
  findings in Section 1-8.07 of this chapter, give notice of the applicant’s right
  to appeal the decision, and be sent to the applicant by first-class mail with
  return receipt requested.

  3. Conditions of Approval. The Review Authority may impose any conditions
  on the approval of an RA Request that he or she deems reasonably
  necessary to ensure that the Reasonable Accommodation will comply with
  the Required Findings in Section 1-8.07.

  c) Compliance with other Regulations. An approved accommodation does not affect
  any person’s obligations to comply with all other applicable regulations not at issue
  in the requested accommodation.

  d) Confidentiality. Any information identified by an applicant as confidential will be
  retained in a manner so as to respect the privacy rights of the applicant and will
  not be made available for public inspection, unless disclosure is otherwise required
  by state or federal law.

  e) No Public Hearing. A public hearing is not required for a reasonable
  accommodation request reviewed and decided upon by the Review Authority.

  f)  No Transfer. An approved accommodation related to property is considered a
  personal RA Request by the applicant, shall not run with the land, and cannot be
  transferred to another person.

§ 1-8.01 Intent.
[ 1, Ord. 1106-11, eff. March 31, 2011; § 3, Ord. 1132-14 eff. November6, 2014]
The purpose of the City of Avalon’s (“City’s’) Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990
(“ADA”) Reasonable Modification Policy is to ensure disabled persons have equal and
effective access to City programs and services, and that reasonable and long-term
modifications to City employment, building, and zoning rules, regulations, practices, and
standards may be made for disabled persons in full compliance with the provisions of Title
II of the ADA and all other applicable State and Federal laws.

§ 1-8.02 Policy Statement.
[ 1, Ord. 1106-11, eff. March 31, 2011; § 3, Ord. No. 1132-14, eff. November 6, 2014]
The City is committed to providing equal access and opportunity to qualified individuals
with disabilities in all City programs, services, employment policies, and building and
zoning rules, regulations, practices, and standards. The City recognizes that in order to
have equally effective opportunities and benefits, individuals with disabilities may need
reasonable and long-term modifications to City policies and procedures. The City will
adhere to all applicable Federal and State laws, regulations and guidelines with respect
to providing reasonable modifications, as necessary, to afford disabled persons equal
access to City programs and services, and to modify City employment, building, and
zoning rules, regulations, practices, and standards when necessary. Questions regarding
reasonable modification and/or discrimination on the basis of disability should be directed
to the City’s ADA Coordinator. A notification of this policy shall be on display at City
Hall/Planning Department to alert people that this policy exists and that a copy of this
policy will be made available by the City upon request.

The City shall make reasonable modifications in policies, practices, or procedures when
the modifications are necessary to avoid discrimination on the basis of disability, unless
the City can demonstrate that making the modifications would fundamentally alter the
nature of the service, program, activity, regulation or policy being modified, or result in an
undue financial or administrative burden.

The City shall take appropriate steps to ensure that communication with applicants,
participants, and members of the public with disabilities are as effective as
communications with others. To this end, the City shall furnish upon request appropriate
auxiliary aids and services where necessary to afford an individual with a disability an
equal opportunity to participate in, and enjoy the benefits of, a service, program, or activity
conducted by the City. In determining what type of auxiliary aid or service is necessary,
the City shall give primary consideration to the requests of the individual with a disability.

The City recognizes that providing services in an integrated setting through architectural
barrier removal is the most desirable method to provide equally effective opportunities
and benefits for many individuals with disabilities.

The City is not required to take any action that it can demonstrate would result in a
fundamental alteration in the nature of a service, program, activity or regulations, or any
action that would result in undue financial or administrative burdens. Any determination
that a modification in its policies or procedures to provide an equal opportunity to
participate in, and enjoy the benefits of, a service, program, or activity for individuals with
disabilities would fundamentally alter the service, program, or activity or unduly burden
the City shall be made by the City ADA Coordinator after consulting with the City Attorney
and after considering all resources available for use in funding and operating the program,
service, or activity. The decision shall be accompanied by a written statement of the
reasons for reaching that determination.

When barrier removal is “technically infeasible” or when reasonable modification would
result in “undue financial or administrative burden” or “fundamental alteration in the nature
of a service, program, or activity,” the procedures in this policy will help ensure that the
City adheres to the requirements of the ADA regulations and guidelines with respect to
burden and infeasibility.

REPORT SUMMARY: For a period of more than 50 years, the City has contracted with a
waterside permit holder for the annual installation, maintenance and operation of the Shore Boat
End Float located at the base of the Green Pleasure Pier.

The Shore Boat End Float performs an essential function in Avalon Harbor, allowing for
additional dock, ticketing and retail space for recreational operations from approximately May 1
to October 15 annually the height of the Summer Season.
  —

After a competitive RFP process, the Lease Agreement for the Shore Boat Float was awarded

new companies under his ownership/control.

of the semi-exclusive shore boat franchise agreement (expiring March 15, 2027) was assigned
to Avalon Shoreboat Services Corporation. The remaining initial term of the Shore Boat Float
Lease Agreement (expiring May 1, 2030) was assigned to Jet Ski Rental Corporation.

Gorelczenko regarding potential sale of the Shore Boat Float and assignment of the remaining

REPORT SUMMARY: During the February 18, 2025 City Council Meeting, the City authorized
the City Manager to execute a Term Sheet with Magical Cruise Company Ltd, dba Disney Cruise
Lines. The City Council additionally authorized the City Manager to negotiate an Agreement with
Disney Cruise Lines incorporating the terms as set forth in the approved Term Sheet.

At this time, negotiations with Disney Cruise Lines have resulted in an agreement addressing
and incorporating all of the relevant terms previously established. Staff recommends authorizing
the City Manager to execute a Preferred Access Agreement with Disney Cruise Lines with the
following terms:

  -  Initial term length of five years commencing upon execution of the Agreement and ending
  September 14, 2030, with two additional five-year renewal options.
  -  Preferential scheduling for Saturdays and Tuesdays during the “Peak Season”
  (September 15 to May 15).
  -  Preferential scheduling for Tuesdays during the “Summer Season” (May 16 to September
  14).
  -  Disney Cruise Lines proposes to remit a Cruise Line Fee equal to the City Wharfage Rate
  plus an additional Passenger Service Charge equal to twenty percent (20%) of the
  Wharfage Rate for each passenger on the manifest as consideration for preferential
  scheduling.
  o This rate will be subject to annual adjustments equal to 2.5% per year.
  -  Disney Cruise Lines shall guarantee a minimum of 120,000 passenger visits to the City
  per year.
  o In the event of a shortfall in any given year, Disney Cruise Lines will remit payment
  at the current wharfage rate plus the applicable “Passenger Service Charge” set
  forth in the Agreement.

At this time, Disney Cruise Lines has two vessels on the West Coast Disney Magic and Disney
  —

Wonder. Both vessels have a maximum passenger capacity of approximately 3,000 passengers.
Though the capacity of these vessels is significantly less than the capacity of other cruise ships
 that currently visit Avalon, the proposed increased wharfage rate and Passenger Service Fee is
anticipated to offset any potential loss of wharfage revenue associated with diminished
passenger counts. Additionally, smaller capacity ships may provide an overall more enjoyable
experience for passengers as well as other Island visitors and residents. The reduced crowds
will result in less congestion, greater activity opportunities, and quicker queuing at the Cabrillo
Mole.

All port agreements entered with any cruise line will align with City of Avalon Resolution No. 24-
34 a resolution that establishes guidelines for approving cruise ship visitation in Avalon.
  —

Per the resolution:
  • Number of regularly scheduled cruise ship vessels shall not exceed 3 per week during
  the Summer Season (Memorial Day to Labor Day) without final written approval of the
  City Manager and Harbor Master.
  • No cruise ship vessels shall be allowed on the weekends during the Summer Season
  (Memorial Day to Labor Day) or during special event weekends such as Jazz Traxx
  —  —

  without final written approval of the City Manager and Harbor Master.
  • Number of regularly scheduled cruise ship vessels shall not exceed 3 per week during
  the “Off Season” (Labor Day to Memorial Day) without final written approval of the City
  Manager and Harbor Master.
  • Repositioning, infrequent, or small cruise ship vessels (1,000 passengers or less) may be
  considered for visitation by the Harbor Master, taking into account the day requested,
  holidays, event(s), harbor activity(ies), impacts to public safety, etc.

City Staff anticipate returning to City Council in the near future with final port agreements with
additional cruise line partners.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Staff anticipate the action may have a net neutral effect on future fiscal year
wharfage revenue projections.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City of Avalon will
not have a port agreement with Disney Cruise Lines.

approximately 1,400 residential and commercial parcels within the city limits. These utilities
operate as enterprise funds, where rates and fees within each fund are set to cover the costs
of providing the respective services to customers. The process for increasing rates is subject
to Proposition 218. HDR performed the last cost of service study for these enterprise funds in
June 2021. The most recent cost of service study included adopted service fees for the
enterprise funds covering five (5) fiscal years ending June 30, 2026.

saltwater, and solid waste rates, including grease collection, supported by a cost of service

equitable, cost-based, and defendable. The City issued the RFP on Thursday, July 3, 2025
with proposals due by Wednesday, August 20, 2025 at 4:00 PM. The City received one bid by

2025 to the four firms solicited and further extended the deadline to Thursday, September 18,

deadline.

REPORT SUMMARY: On October 22, 2024, the City Council approved the design plan and
authorized procurement for Stage 0 of the Cabrillo Mole Revitalization Project.

The Cabrillo Mole Ferry Terminal is a multimodal transportation hub used by cross-channel
carrier passengers traveling between the City and the mainland, cruise ship
disembarkmentlembarkment, and serves as the primary entry point to the City. In 2020, the City
completed Phase 1 of the Cabrillo Mole Rehabilitation Project which included the rehabilitation
and reinforcement of the existing concrete members, replacement of the steel grates, and
repaired the concrete deck and railing for a total project cost of $5.10 million.
  —

The next portion of the project, budgeted at $20 million, will replace and reconfigure the existing
building and structures to improve passenger queuing and adjacent transportation circulation.

In order to accommodate sustained, mostly uninterrupted operations of the Cabrillo Mole,
construction of the new facility has been broken into 10 construction stages. The Pre
Construction Stage Stage 0 includes four steps. The first step will complete a scope of work
  —  —

associated with the Phase 1 project as well as include installation of grates at the old steamer
ramp ways along the easterly face of the Mole wharf.

This portion of the project utilized a competitive procurement as outlined in Avalon Municipal
Code Section 3-4.106(d). The City solicited a request for bids (RFB) from qualified contractors
to complete the Phase I scope of work as well as install grates over the top of two existing cut
outs along the easterly face of the Mole. These grates will allow construction and emergency
vehicles an approximate twenty-foot pathway so they may access the full length of the mole
throughout the construction project. The grates will become a permanent addition to the mole
wharf.
 The RFB was published on the City’s website, www.CityofAvalon.gov/rfp, as well as on Public
Purchase on August 28, 2025. A non-mandatory pre-bid meeting was held on site and virtually
on Thursday September 4. Only one prospective bidder attended the meeting.

The bid deadline was extended by request of a prospective bidder on September 11. The bidding
deadline officially closed on Monday September 15 at 4 p.m. The City received one bid by the
stated deadline from Slater Waterproofing, Inc. In addition to being the only bidder to submit,
Slater Waterproofing, Inc. completed the initial Phase I scope of work making them an excellent
contractor for this project as they are already familiar with the facility, varying weather conditions
that may be presented and other logistical nuances.

City Staff recommends the City Council awards the contract to complete Cabrillo Mole
Revitalization Project Phase I Remainder of Work and Phase II Wharf Infill Project to Slater
  —  —

Waterproofing, Inc. for a not-to-exceed sum of $950,000.

City Staff anticipates this project will be completed by early 2026.

The procurement process for the remaining three scopes of work associated with Stage 0 are
all underway. Staff anticipate returning to City Council in the forthcoming months to award
contracts for the (1) installation of utility systems and other temporary infrastructure to support
the future Cabrillo Mole facility as well as temporary facilities, (2) purchase of long-lead
equipment associated with the upgraded utility system, as well as (3) purchase temporary
facilities.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Undetermined.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City will not have a
plan to support the construction of the Cabrillo Mole Project.

the Civic Center Housing Project, authorizing Phase 1 in the amount of $55,000, with
direction to return to Council prior to issuance of Phase 2.

As part of Phase 1 planning and design work, it has been determined that a traffic and
logistics study is necessary to evaluate the transport of oversized modular housing units
from the barge landing through the City to the Civic Center campus. This analysis will
ensure safe delivery of units, identify any necessary traffic control or infrastructure
modifications, and provide the City with a traffic engineering report for review.

US-Offsite, in collaboration with K2 Traffic Engineering, has submitted a proposal to
provide this work at a fixed fee of $6,995. The proposal includes:
  • Evaluation of transport route and turning movements at six key intersections.
  • Preparation of a Caltrans permit application.
  • Development of a detailed logistics plan including transport, staging, and craning.
  • On-island site visit and coordination with City staff.

The traffic study will provide critical information for Phase 1 deliverables and help ensure
the feasibility of transporting modular units to the project site.

FISCAL IMPACTS: There is adequate funding allocated in Capital Project 205014 Civic
Center Housing Project for FY2025-26.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Improve local housing.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: Without this
study, the City risks delays or unforeseen challenges in the delivery of modular units,
potentially impacting project feasibility and schedule.
 FOLLOW UP ACTION: If approved, staff will execute the amendment and proceed with
the traffic study in coordination with US-Offsite and K2 Traffic Engineering.

SUBJECT:  Short-Term Rental Application Waitlist Policy Discussion

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Hear a presentation regarding policy options for processing
short-term rental application after the maximum number of licenses have been issued. If
consensus, provide direction to City Staff.

BACKGROUND: On August 9, 2025, The City Council introduced and waived all further
readings of an ordinance repealing and replacing Article 3 of Chapter 1 of Title 3 of the Avalon
Municipal Code modifying the Transient Rental System. This ordinance was adopted at the
September 2, 2025 regular City Council meeting and went into effect on October 1, 2025.

Per the City Council’s direction, the ordinance established a cap of 410 transient rental units
within the City of Avalon. This cap includes all grand-fathered transient rental units, all units with
conditional use permits and all units with transient rental licenses.

The City has identified a total of 386 compliant short-term rental properties, including:
  • 91 properties permitted by grandfathered use (including 9 banked units currently occupied
  by year-round renters),
  • 267 properties permitted by CUP (including 13 banked units currently occupied by year-
  round renters), and
  • 28 properties permitted by Transient Business License (including 1 banked units currently
  occupied by year-round renters).

Due to the newly established limit on new transient rental license permits, the ordinance
authorizes the City Manager to implement a policy to regulate the manner in which the Planning
Commission considers new transient rental license once that limit is reached.

After conducting an informal survey of four cities with ordinances or policies that limit the number
of transient rental licenses, staff have developed two main options for the City Council to con
sider establishing a first come, first served waitlist, or develop a lottery system.
  —

Lottery System
The City of San Diego is one of four cities surveyed that limits the number of un-hosted short
term rental licenses, and has reached that limit on the number of issued licenses in an area. San
 Diego utilizes a lottery system to determine how to prioritize and process short term rental occu
pancy licenses.

Referencing the City of San Diego as a model, City Staff recommend the following procedure
for consideration of TRL applications.

  -  Annually, assuming there are TRLs available under the cap, or at any time there are five
  or more available TRLs, the City will open an application period for 60 days to allow for
  the submittal of TRL applications.
  -  At the conclusion of the application period, an independent department will perform a
  random lottery to determine the waitlist position of all valid and complete applications.
  -  After the lottery, the applicants are notified and prioritized in the order established by the
  lottery.
  -  Applications are heard by the Planning Commission in the order established by the lottery.
  -  Once all available TRLs are filled under the cap, all remaining applications are rejected.

In addition to establishing a general lottery system, Staff propose creating a weighted/priority
point system where added points are applied to owners who have long-term rental properties,
or have participated in previous lotteries and been rejected.

Staff recommend a lottery system to determine waitlist priority for the following reasons:
  • Reduces administrative burden by establishing a finite window for the receipt and
  processing of transient rental license applications.
  • Allows for all interested property owners to have an equal opportunity to receive a TRL.
  • It may disincentivize property investors from purchasing property on speculation.
  • It disincentivizes transient rental license seekers from abusing the complaint system.
  • Avoids the creation of a multi-year list that continues to grow annually and becomes overly
  burdensome to manage or monitor.
  • Eliminates the property value increase for properties that are “next” or in the “top 10” of
  the waitlist.
  • Could potentially provide opportunities to incentivize long-term rentals while waiting.

First Come, First Serve Waitlist
Three of the four cities surveyed that have both a limit to the number of short-term rental
licenses/permits, and have reached that limit, have established a standard first come, first served
waitlist.

A first come first served waitlist would be beneficial as it could provide priority to those that have
been on the waitlist the longest, and reduce the uncertainty of not knowing the status of the
property owner’s application.

If a First Come, First Served Policy is adopted, waitlist policy should include:
  -  A requirement for property owners to keep contact information current with the City by
  way of payment of an annual feel. (Similar to the leased mooring list in Avalon Harbor.)
  -  Waitlist positions are not transferable.
  -  Waitlist positions would be forfeited if property is sold or transferred.
 A discussion was held with the Planning Commission at the September 17, 2025 Planning
Commission Meeting. A consensus was reached among the commissioners to recommend the
City Council considers a lottery waitlist policy that allows for weighting for applicants that have
long-term rental units and/or participated in past lotteries and were not selected.

If consensus is reached, City Staff will develop a complete policy and procedure and bring it
back to City Council at a future meeting for adoption by resolution.
